<description>
I've tested some mutations related to test coverage for PSBT unknown field merging and discovered an inconsistency.

If line 71 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(psbt.unknown.begin(), psbt.unknown.end());`"  (inside `bool PartiallySignedTransaction::Merge(const PartiallySignedTransaction& psbt)` function) is removed then, the expected test fails: *"Test that combining PSBTs preserves unknown fields with the same and with distinct values per map."*

If line 434 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(input.unknown.begin(), input.unknown.end());`" (inside `bool PSBTInput::Merge(const PSBTInput& input)` function), is removed, a different unexpected test fails: "*Test that unknown values are just passed through*".

If line 537 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(output.unknown.begin(), output.unknown.end());`" (inside `bool PSBTOutput::Merge(const PSBTOutput& output)` function), is removed, the expected test fails: "*Test that combining PSBTs preserves unknown fields with the same and with distinct values per map.*".

This PR solves this inconsistency.
The old code did 3 different things:
1. Test the pass-through of unknown values for `walletprocesspsbt`.
2. Combine two v0 PSBTs with different unknown input keys and check that both keys survive.
3. Combine implicit v0 PSBT with explicit v0 and check that both keys survive.

Case 2 is already fully covered by the existing `test_combinepsbt_preseves_unknown_fields` so keeping it is redundant and misleading.

Commit 40eba5eb20ba0041a6328ba3482fcc26ddbe0185 moves the old code into a new method called `test_unknown_fields_passthrough` and commit ef4310097bd651497a98a9d1bb59560a7055ae01 removes the redundant code of Case 2 and moves Case 3 inside `test_combinepsbt_preserves_unknown_fields`.
</description>

<commits>

ef4310097b test: combine redundant PSBT unknown field merge cases into `test_combinepsbt_preserves_unknown_fields`
